document_title: More Than 600 Were Citizens. About 1,900 Never Answered
post_copy:
Alaska's elections director told lawmakers more than 600 citizens came off the active voter list and she won't restore them herself.

Both sit in one August 6th letter that promises another notice with no date on it. The primary is August 18th.

In 2024 the DMV and the Division of Elections compared just 2,000 records. More than 580,000 were compared this year. The DMV called that non-routine, per the Alaska Beacon.

That letter posts as three images with no text layer, so its figures reach the public through one newsroom's reading.

The four reported outcomes at one scale. Both published totals with outlet and date. Four things a removed voter can still do.

About 1,900 people never answered and no published account says how many of them are citizens. Against 580,000 records compared, what is more than 600 a measure of?

#AlaskaElections #VoterRolls #AKpol

Note on sourcing. The elections director's August 6th letter is published on elections.alaska.gov as three images with no text layer, so the figures in this deck reach the public through the Alaska Beacon's reading of that letter. Two outlets report different totals for the number of registrations moved, 3,048 and 3,058, and no page reconciles them, so the deck prints both with their outlet and date rather than choosing one.

caption_meta.deck_summary: The four reported outcomes at one scale. Both published totals with outlet and date. Four things a removed voter can still do.
caption_meta.note: The caption room killed BOTH first candidates. Each had invented a mechanism the record does not describe, that the more than 600 were found because they wrote back. C01 states plainly that 600 is not the count who contacted the Division. The reassigned round holds the two populations apart and never explains how the 600 were identified.

aftercare: Post Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time.
Paste the first comment immediately, inside sixty seconds, so the sources are up before the first readers arrive.
Reply substantively to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. A dead first hour is rarely recovered.
This deck carries a deadline that expires August 8th. If it is not posted before then, slide 08's first line is stale and the deck should be reviewed before posting.
If a commenter asks whether the 1,900 are citizens, the honest answer is that nobody knows and no published account says.
Do not let a reply describe this as an AI system. Four outlets and the agencies' own joint statement all call it a comparison of two record sets.
